headline: No direct interaction pathway is documented; the main residual risk is low-probability data/workflow interference between two read-only, non-networked data-engineering components.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Neither agent exposes a shared communication channel, clipboard, filesystem, MCP, or stdin/stdout bridge. Dagster is documented with no filesystem write, read, browser, subprocess, or MCP surfaces; RisingWave only shows no network egress. Without an ingestion path, prompt injection between them is not plausible.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator adds a shared clipboard, filesystem, or message queue between the agents, injection risk becomes possible.
mitigations: Keep the agents isolated with no shared transport.
Disable any future clipboard or file handoff between them.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging if a bridge is introduced.

B_data_leakage.rationale: The profiles show no touched data classes, no filesystem sharing, and no network egress for either agent. Dagster cannot read or write files, and RisingWave also has no egress. With no documented data path, leakage from one to the other is not supported by the profiles.
conditions: IF either agent is later granted shared workspace access or file-reading capability, leakage risk must be re-evaluated.
mitigations: Keep sensitive data out of any shared workspace.
Review future permission changes before deployment.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: There is no overlapping write surface to conflict over: Dagster cannot write the filesystem or modify git state, and RisingWave exposes no write or concurrency surface in the profile. Because the pair lacks a shared mutable resource, capability conflict is not evidenced.
conditions: IF either agent gains write access to the same directory, database, or git repository, conflict risk may emerge.
mitigations: requires-engineering: add locking if shared state is introduced.

D_cascading_error.rationale: No pathway shows one agent consuming the other's outputs as authoritative input. Dagster has no stdin/stdout or file surfaces, and RisingWave has no documented action-taking authority here. Without an output-to-input bridge, cascading error is not plausible from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF an orchestrator starts piping Dagster outputs into RisingWave decisions without verification, cascading error risk appears.
mitigations: Insert a human or rule-based verification step.
Do not auto-act on generated outputs.
requires-engineering: add schema validation before any downstream action.

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance-sensitive data classes are listed for either agent, and both profiles show no network egress. The profiles do not indicate residency, retention, or certification mismatches, so no compliance breach pathway is evidenced. The other agent is not separately cited because no data class or jurisdictional flow is documented.
conditions: IF either agent begins processing regulated data such as PHI or EU PII, compliance review is required.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair.
requires-engineering: add residency and retention controls if regulated data is introduced.
